scenario: Quick battle seed 517a27ed; direct terrain seeds 291 plus pixel matrix; real host first rocket; native windowed/null audio

method.order: A B repeated; every capture has its own bench lease
method.acceptance: At least 5% primary median improvement and at least 80% pair direction, or separated distributions; correctness and CPU/RSS/GUI/file-size guards must pass.

experiments.hypothesis: Per-byte Ruby PNG filtering dominates tile encoding.
experiments.change: Use guarded byte lanes in row-sized Ruby integers; retain palettes and zlib settings.
experiments.reason: 11.36% faster match start, 5/5 pairs; exact PNG bytes; RSS and GUI maximum guards pass.

experiments.hypothesis: Decoding the baked texture kit dominates the first paint.
experiments.change: Decode RGBA average-filtered rows four channels per integer, with standard decoding fallback.
experiments.reason: 13.21% further match-start reduction, 5/5 pairs; every texture and painted pixel identical; resource/GUI guards pass.

experiments.hypothesis: Four forked painters can finish disjoint tiles sooner.
experiments.change: Preload the kit, fork at most four children for large batches, merge ordered tile/minimap results.
experiments.reason: 20.99% faster start, but aggregate peak RSS doubles in all five pairs. RSS counts shared copy-on-write pages; physical memory is not claimed to double.

experiments.hypothesis: One integer pass per image could avoid most row allocations.
experiments.change: Apply the same exact-byte UP filter across the complete image.
experiments.reason: Painter wall time is 3.18% worse in all five pairs; direct-workload RSS rises substantially.

experiments.hypothesis: Eight-row batches could reduce temporary allocations within a smaller bound.
experiments.change: Apply guarded UP subtraction to eight-row strips.
experiments.reason: Median wall time is 0.11% worse, only 2/5 faster; peak sampled direct RSS rises from 90,032 to 130,280 KiB.

additional_checks.extra_seed_matrix: 28 maps, 84 renders per arm; decoded pixels and tile bytes match

limits: Linux x86-64 Ruby 3.4.7 source runs; no Darwin execution, device audio, compositor scanout or physical Mac claim.
App captures use Xvfb, native completion barriers, a fixed Quick battle seed, OpenAL null audio and warm/uncontrolled file caches.
Peak game-process RSS is sampled every 50 ms, summed over GUI, native renderer, host and all painters; it includes shared pages and may miss brief peaks.
GUI frame metrics are App#update durations and intervals, not every GUI callback or presented display frames.

The first-shot explosion endpoint starts at host explode entry; request latency starts at enqueue completion. Both end at the 60 Hz result poll and include delivery/poll phase effects. Request-to-ready stays near 100 ms; this is not a demonstrated general per-shot speedup.

Worker allocation count and GC work increase (60,170 to 159,415 allocations; 23.60 to 43.41 ms GC in the native initial render), while total worker CPU, wall time and peak RSS improve. GC is isolated from the GUI.
Hard parent SIGKILL leaves the existing temporary directory; the lifecycle harness removes it after proving the worker exits. Normal close and repeated matches remove directories.
No protocol, simulation, checkpoint, worker/readiness, framework, asset or runtime-setting change is included.
open_proposals: Defer transient Quick battle lobby-preview generation with the app/screens owner; the largest loading GUI update remains around 170 ms.

Visible-first readiness needs camera coverage gating and collision/visible-terrain guarantees. The current Scene marks the first result ready and permits immediate overview/panning, so partial tiles would expose holes. No progressive prototype was shipped.
Consider build-time texture encoding/predecoding if the remaining roughly 0.95 s cold kit decode merits asset/generator scope and package-size measurements.
Validate the packaged Ruby 3.4.7 build on Apple silicon before making Mac performance or audio claims.
